All animate and inanimate entities, both natural and supernatural, either created or pre-existent before creation, either existing in nature or human-made.
All objects found in the regions above the earth.
All supernatural beings.
All celestial bodies found in the regions above the earth, such as sun, moon, stars, constellations, etc.
All objects found on the earth.
All terms related to land in its relation to the people living there or those engaging with it in other ways.
All landforms, such as mountains, valleys, plains.
All terms for different landscapes, such as forests, deserts, etc.
All vegetation.
All plants.
All trees.
All terms for bodies of water on the earth, such as oceans, seas, lakes, rivers, and ponds.
All living creatures, with the exception of created supernatural beings and humans.
All wild land animals of the larger variety, excluding smaller animals, such as the mouse or the weasel, which, according to Lev. 11:29, are to be considered |uSmall Animals|u*.
All domesticated animals.

All wild land animals of the smaller variety. According to Genesis 1:24 this is a category in itself. It does somewhat overlap with שֶׁרֶץ, however. Leviticus 11:29 refers to (part of) this subcategory of animals as שֶׁרֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל־הָאָרֶץ which refers to all land animals that have short legs (reptiles) or no legs at all (snakes). To use the term reptiles would be incorrect as small mammals, such as the mouse and the weasel, are part of this subcategory as well.
All water creatures except what is considered שֶׁרֶץ הַמַּיִם (see Swarming Creatures). See Leviticus 11:9-12; Deuteronomy 14:9,10.
All birds, covered by the Hebrew generic term עוֹף. Flying insects are part of the category Swarming Creatures.

All animals covered by the generic term שֶׁרֶץ, with the exception of the reptiles and small rodents that are classified as רֶמֶשׂ Small Animals. This comprises what is referred to as שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף (Lev. 11:20), שֶׁרֶץ הַמַּיִם (Lev. 11:10), and probably the smaller species of the שֶׁרֶץ הַשֹׂרֵץ עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Lev. 11:29).
All human beings.
All social classes among humans, such as slave, free, alien, rich, poor, etc.
All humans with whom one has a hostile relationship—for example, enemies, opponents, or adversaries.
All humans with whom one has a positive relationship—for example, friends, companions, or partners.
All groups of humans not mentioned under any of the other categories.
All humans that are in a position of authority over others, e.g. kings, commanders, officers, prefects, etc.
All humans that are commissioned to pass on a message to others.
All humans that are in the service of a king or other leader.
All humans functioning as priests or hold another religious office.
All people engaged in a certain professional activity, such as farmers, craftsmen, fishermen, etc.
All humans speaking or acting on behalf of a deity, e.g. seers and prophets.
All humans, both male and female, who engage in non-sanctioned sexual relationships, whether professionally or occasionally.
All humans that are related by blood or marriage.
All humans engaged in military activities, e.g. warriors, soldiers, officers, etc.
All humans giving testimony in courts or other legal contexts.

All inanimate objects, usually of a relatively small size, produced by people, deities, animals, or plants. An important characteristic of this category is that this type of objects can be actively used as instruments in other processes. In figures of speech objects of this category often take the place of the events in which they are used as instruments.
All human-made objects.
All flags, banner, standards and other objects that function as visible signs.
All terms referring to clothing and armor.
All objects produced to contain other objects such as liquids or dry substances.
All objects used to keep other objects in place, such as cords, chains, fetters and similar objects.
All objects that are used to cover other objects, such as the lid of a jar, the coverings of the tabernacle, or a saddle-cloth to ride on. For clothes, see Clothing.
All objects that are the object of worship, such as idols, scared pillars, sacred poles,etc.
All objects that generate and contain heat—typically by burning fuel—for heating, cooking, or baking.
All objects used to furnish and decorate the inside of buildings.
All precious stones.
All objects that are visual representations of deities, humans, or other objects, either or not used for worship.
All jewellery, such as rings, necklaces, etc.
All human-made objects used for producing light in a certain area.
All musical instruments.
All terms for writing equipment and objects holding written text, such as scrolls, tablets, seals, etc.
All vehicles used for travel and transportation over water.
All visible signs, such as flags, banners, standards and other objects that function as visible signs.
All objects used by craftsmen to produce artifacts.
All instruments used for hunting and fishing. These objects are often used in a metaphorical sense to denote devices used by evil people to ensnare others.
All vehicles used for travel and transportation over land.
All artifacts used in warfare, ranging from small hand-held arms to large siege-works.
All body products, such as excrement, sweat, semen, blood, etc.

All terms for food items. It must be noted that many food items can be regarded as substances as well. Honey, for instance, is both a food product and a substance. That fact that it is a substance, however, seems to be less relevant than its membership of of the food category.
All baked food products made out of grain.
All crops growing as plants, such as grain, wheat, barley, flax, etc.
All food produced by animals, such as dairy products, but also eggs and honey.
All edible objects produced by plants and trees.
All terms for wine and other alcoholic beverages.
All inanimate objects that are immovable and constructed by humans, such as huts, shelters, houses, fortresses, and palaces. For larger population centers such as towns and villages, see |uTowns|u.
All permanent constructions not covered by any of the other categories at this level.
All places where religious activities are concentrated, such as shrines, temples, high places, etc.
All constructions that serve to fortify a city.
All constructions erected to serve as a memorial for a certain person or event.
All places where ships find shelter and can be loaded or unloaded.
All constructions where people are incarcerated.
All infrastructural constructions that facilitate travel and transportation from one place to the other.
All constructions where domestic animals are kept
All temporary constructions, such as tents, shelters, etc.
All terms referring to burial places.
All population centers, such as villages and towns.
All constructions surrounding an area, building, compound, or population center.
All constructions were water is drawn from the ground or stored.

All inanimate objects that are shaped in such a way that they usually cannot be counted but are to be measured instead, and from which other objects can be produced, e.g. gold, silver, wood, clay, etc. This category includes liquids like water, and elements like fire. These objects are either exclusively used in the singular, or in the shape of a fixed plural or dual form
All terms referring to the air and the movement of air, e.g. wind, breeze, storm, etc.
All terms related to bitumen and other petroleum-based materials.
All terms for cloth and the materials used for making clothes, such as linen and wool
All terms related to clouds.
All small particles covering the earth, such as dust, ashes, soot, sand, etc.
All terms related to fire, except smoke.
All liquids.
All metals, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, lead, etc.
All terms for minerals, such as salt and sulphur.
All terms for substances used to apply color to other objects.
All forms of precipitation, such as rain, hail, snow.
All terms referring to the gases and vapors produced by fire.
All substances used to facilitate the removal of dirt from people and objects.
All terms for substances such as fragrant spices, powders, and ointments used for culinary, medicinal, and cosmetic purposes.
All types of stones, rocks, and pebbles; for precious stones, see: |uGemstones|u*.
All terms for wood as a product.
All terms relating to the regions under the earth, such as the subterranean waters, the world of the dead, etc.

All states, processes, actions, and causative actions, featuring one or more objects or other events. States and Processes overlap in biblical Hebrew and are therefore considered one single category in SDBH (State/Process). Terms that are often labeled abstracts or attributes in semantic theory function as states in biblical Hebrew and are therefore considered events

Events that describe features of objects or other events. This includes certain adjectives and adverbs, words that according to Nida's analysis usually classify as abstracts rather than events. In biblical Hebrew, however, the distinction between events and abstracts does not work very well, as there is much overlap between the two semantic classes
